alpha-msh.definition: A small natural hormone made in the body from a larger protein. It controls skin and hair colour and also calms inflammation. KPV is its last three building blocks.

proopiomelanocortin.definition: A large protein the body cuts into several smaller hormones, including alpha-MSH and a stress hormone called ACTH.

tripeptide.definition: A peptide made of exactly three amino acids joined in a chain. KPV is a tripeptide: lysine, proline and valine.

melanocortin-receptor.definition: A set of receptors on cells that alpha-MSH switches on. One of them, in skin cells, controls pigment. KPV does not appear to bind these receptors.

nf-kb.definition: A control switch inside cells that turns on many inflammation genes. When it moves into the cell's nucleus, the cell makes more inflammatory signals.

cytokine.definition: A small signalling protein that immune cells release to start or spread inflammation. Examples are TNF-α and interleukin-1β.

pept1.definition: A doorway protein on the surface of gut and some immune cells that carries small peptides of two or three amino acids into the cell. It is scarce in a healthy colon but increases when the colon is inflamed.

myeloperoxidase.definition: An enzyme carried by neutrophils, a type of white blood cell. Measuring it in tissue is a common way to estimate how many of these inflammatory cells are present.

inflammatory-bowel-disease.definition: A group of long-term diseases, mainly ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease, in which the gut becomes inflamed. They need medical treatment.

dss-colitis.definition: A way of giving mice or rats a bowel inflammation on purpose, usually by putting a chemical (such as dextran sodium sulfate) in their drinking water, so that treatments can be tested.

pharmacophore.definition: The part of a molecule that is responsible for its main action. In alpha-MSH, a different part controls pigment from the part that calms inflammation.

stratum-corneum.definition: The thin, tough outer layer of the skin. It is a barrier that keeps most large or water-loving molecules, including peptides, from passing into the body.

in-vitro.definition: An experiment done outside a living body, for example in cells grown in a dish. Latin for "in glass".

in-vivo.definition: An experiment done in a living body, such as a mouse or a person. Latin for "in the living".
